label: tai
title: たい
meaning_example: I want to see a Bond movie!

examples.japanese: ボンドの映画を見たいな〜。
examples.body_text:
ボンドの映画を見たいな〜。 

		I 
		wanna 
		see the Bond movie!
examples.body_html:
ボンドの映画を見たいな〜。 
I wanna see the Bond movie!

examples.japanese: この車を買いたいんですが、お金が無い。
examples.body_text:
この車を買いたいんですが、お金が無い。 

		I 
		want to buy 
		this car but I don't have the money.
examples.body_html:
この車を買いたいんですが、お金が無い。 
I want to buy this car but I don't have the money.

examples.japanese: あなたは何をしたいのですか。
examples.body_text:
あなたは何をしたいのですか。 

		What would you like to do?
examples.body_html:
あなたは何をしたいのですか。 
What would you like to do?

examples.japanese: 彼女は私のすることをいつみ知りたがる。
examples.body_text:
彼女は私のすることをいつみ知りたがる。 

		She`s always curious about (as to) what I`m doing.
examples.body_html:
彼女は私のすることをいつみ知りたがる。 
She`s always curious about (as to) what I`m doing.

comments.text:
Note that when speaking of what somebody else wants you should use the -がる form. E.g. たい→たがる.  Basically you shouldn't say "She wants to ___" but "She looks like she wants to ___".



In asking questions the direct 〜たい form is fine.
comments.html:
Note that when speaking of what somebody else wants you should use the -がる form. E.g. たい→たがる. Basically you shouldn't say "She wants to ___" but "She looks like she wants to ___".

In asking questions the direct 〜たい form is fine.

comments.text: In modern Japanese 〜たい generally takes を with が being used for emphasis when strong feelings are involved.
comments.html: In modern Japanese 〜たい generally takes を with が being used for emphasis when strong feelings are involved.

  noun + wo / ga Verb-masu base + tai



Vm = Verb -masu base

comments.text: な〜 is express your feeling by put 〜 written sentence. You can also write 見たいな。見たいな〜。見たいよ〜。見たいね！

comments.text: From what I've heard (and seen used), 〜たい / 〜ほしい is used even when referring to other people, because it's regarded more polite than 〜がる forms. This might be limited only to 2nd person, though, I'm not completely sure.
